evidence: Four independent probes agree. (1) A 4096-vocab BPE was trained with train_tokenizer on generator text with code at about 1/8 of the sample, like build.py:200-218. The prompt tail is ['."""', 'Ċ'], while prompt+reference gives ['."""', 'ĊĠĠĠ', 'Ġreturn', ...]. For 50/50 function items the prompt tokens are not a prefix of the prompt+reference tokens. The same check over every other non-chat item (reasoning, pattern, knowledge, consistency, coding outputs) found 0 mismatches. In code training text a bare 'Ċ' was followed by a space-led token 0 times out of about 22k-51k, and a closing docstring was followed by 'ĊĠĠĠ' every time (2011/2011, 1990, 7001/7001 in different probes). (2) Small models (2 layers, 128 wide) were trained on code_train_docs on the CPU. With the suite's prompt 0/50 items pass and replies start 'print(...)'. With the trailing newline removed, 49-50/50 pass and replies start with a newline and an indented 'return'. (3) The fakes (answer_key_lm replies with the reference text; Task 16 fakes keyed by exact token tuples) and the reply-budget test (test_bench.py:707-739) cannot catch this. (4) No ledger, ADR or task-report ruling covers the boundary.
fix: Show the model the header up to the closing quotes with no trailing newline: in _bench_functions build CheckItem(prompt=v.prompt.rstrip('\n'), check_args={'prompt': v.prompt, ...}), or rstrip non-chat prompts in suite._ask/_prompt_ids. function_body already keeps a leading empty line, so a reply starting with a newline builds valid source (50/50 references pass that way). Leave _Variant.prompt and the training docs unchanged, so no corpus rebuild is needed; MEASURING_SOURCES changes, so gate caches refresh. Update fakes.answer_key_lm to use the same encoding and reply with a newline + reference. Add a regression test that, for every non-chat bench item, encode(prompt) + encode(continuation) == encode(prompt + continuation) under a BPE trained with the build's pre-tokenizer (or, more simply, that no non-chat prompt ends in whitespace). Record the deviation from plan line 1176 in ADR 0001. Do it before the owner's first real gate run and before bench-v1 freezes.
line: 878 (_Variant.prompt ends with the docstring's closing quotes plus a newline), 1004-1012 (CheckItem prompt = v.prompt), 927 (training text = prompt + body); consumed at ml/src/airace_ml/evals/suite.py:151-154 and 204-210; checkers.py:152-162; format mandated by plan line 1176
scenario: tok-v1 is byte-level BPE with the GPT-2 pre-tokenizer (tokenizer.py:80). In training text (prompt + body), the newline after a function's docstring always merges with the body's indentation into one token (newline + 3 spaces, 'ĊĠĠĠ'). The bench prompt for each of the 50 fmt:function items ends exactly at that newline, so its last token is a bare 'Ċ'. In the code training text a bare 'Ċ' is only ever followed by column-0 lines ('print', 'Output', 'def', 'for'). A model that has learned to write bodies therefore continues with greedy decoding as `print(add_numbers(5, 16))  # 21`. function_body() cuts at that first unindented line and returns '', MiniPy runs a body that is only the docstring, and every hidden test fails. All 50 function items read 0 for every model whatever it learned. Consequences: coding is capped at about 67, the fmt:function and function-family discovery tags never fire, G3's 'code-heavy mix leads coding' must rest on the output-prediction items alone and can fail for a measurement reason, and bench-v1 would freeze with the defect. The implementation follows the plan's prompt format faithfully, so the plan itself is wrong here.
title: Function-completion bench prompts end on a bare newline token that training never follows with indentation, so no trained model can pass the 50 function items (a third of coding in bench-v1)

evidence: Probes on the frozen streams skill_rng('knowledge'/'consistency', 'bench') and on build_suite(): subject-blind per-relation majority picker hits animal_legs 11/16, animal_class 9/16, baby_animal 7/15, vehicle_travel 7/15, shape_sides 4/10; MC 0.367 (0.371 with random ties), exact 0.26, category score 18.8 via evals.scoring.normalize. ScriptedLM with score = log(1 + KB count) and reply 'four' through run_benchmarks(categories=['knowledge','consistency']) gives knowledge 14.5 (raw 0.305), consistency 0.0. No ledger ruling covers the knowledge answer distribution.
fix: Before bench-v1 freezes: (a) stratify knowledge and consistency fact selection by answer, i.e. within each relation draw the object uniformly (or cap each object at about 1/N_OPTIONS of the relation's items) and then a subject with that object, so the 4-option set is exchangeable and any subject-blind rule gets exactly 1/4; and/or (b) measure a floor as the instruction category does: best per-relation constant reply for exact items, per-relation majority-object accuracy for MC items. Add a regression test that a subject-blind relation-prior model scores within about chance + 0.05 (knowledge normalized about 0) on knowledge and consistency.
line: 46-55 (_sample_facts: uniform over facts within a relation), 68-79 (_bench_pools), 144-165 (knowledge_bench_items), 175 (consistency_groups); ml/src/airace_ml/skills/kb.py:161-178 (distractors uniform over other objects); ml/src/airace_ml/evals/suite.py:170 (MC chance = 1/len(options)), 178 (exact chance 0)
scenario: Bench facts are drawn uniformly within each relation, so true answers follow the KB's object frequencies: 'four' is the answer to 11/16 animal_legs MC items, 'mammal' to 9/16 animal_class, and baby_animal ('calf'), vehicle_travel ('by water') and shape_sides ('four') lean the same way. Distractors are uniform over the other objects. A model that has learned only relation priors ('...legs does a koala have? Answer: four') and no subject facts picks the relation's most common object: 0.367 on MC (assumed chance 0.25) and 26% on exact items (assumed chance 0), a knowledge score of 18.8. A fully question-blind scorer (option score = log KB count, reply 'four' to everything) run through run_benchmarks scores 14.5. Over 30 other bench draws the subject-blind MC rate averages 0.40, so this is systematic. Knowledge reads well above 0 before any fact is known, breaking R5/ADR 0001's '0 means chance' and misleading G3 and players; the gap is larger than the instruction one (14.2) already ruled Important. The Task 16 ruling 'exact items keep chance 0 (best constant 2.5-4%)' tested only one global constant reply, not per-relation constants or MC option priors. consistency_groups uses the same sampler; its frozen draw happens to normalize to 0 (expected value 0.29).
title: Knowledge (and consistency) bench answers follow the KB's skewed base rates while chance is set to 1/options (MC) and 0 (exact), so a model that ignores the subject scores about 15-19 on knowledge
